[E1] 12 CFR § 1026.3(b)(1) and Supplement I, comment 3(b)-5.i (summary). For an unsecured closed-end consumer loan that is not a private education loan, the amount-based exemption applies if the lender extends credit at consummation in an amount exceeding the threshold then in effect, or makes an express written commitment at consummation to extend a total amount exceeding that threshold. Consummation is when the borrower becomes contractually bound to the loan.
[E2] Supplement I, comment 3(b)-3.xv. “From January 1, 2024, through December 31, 2024, the threshold amount is $69,500.”
[E3] Supplement I, comment 3(b)-3.xvi. “From January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025, the threshold amount is $71,900.”

A lender offered a borrower two alternative amounts for a single unsecured, closed-end loan for household expenses. It was not a private education loan. The two options were A ($75,000) and B ($70,000). Under either option, the lender would disburse the entire amount when the borrower became contractually bound, with no commitment to extend any further credit. The loan could only have been consummated on one of the local calendar days from 2024-12-31 through 2025-01-01, inclusive.
The loan was consummated on 2024-12-31.

Would option A qualify for the amount-based exemption under § 1026.3(b)?
The caseworker needs a single determination. If you can give one, state it and cite the applicable evidence by ID. If you need another fact to make that determination, ask for it.
